cases.name: Working contribution and compensation caps

issues.message: planned contributions of 7500 a year at the starting age exceed the earned income of 5000 of the household members contributing, and nothing the plan models funds the difference

The working years are not funded by pay: at age 40 the year's pay, after payroll and income tax, does not cover the contributions and debt payments (with any mortgage insurance) made while working, by about $2,883. The plan has no budget for the working years, so it does not say where that money comes from; check the contributions and debt payments against take-home pay. Pay here is salary and any employment and self-employment income paid while working, net of the payroll, self-employment and income tax it adds.
